newsitem.title: USA: Clinton maintains strong lead over Dole.
newsitem.headline: Clinton maintains strong lead over Dole.

text.p: President Clinton slightly increased his double-digit lead over Republican challenger Bob Dole with nine days to go in the 1996 campaign, according to the Reuters daily tracking poll released on Sunday.
Clinton led Dole by 46.6 percent to 33.2 percent compared to a lead of 46.7 percent to 33.6 percent on Saturday in the poll conducted for Reuters by John Zogby Group International.
Reform Party candidate Perot's support remained at 7.8 percent, while 10.4 percent of respondents said they were undecided.

The tracking poll surveys approximately 900 likely voters over a three-day period, creating a new three-day rolling average each day. Sunday's poll covered on Thursday, Friday and Saturday. The margin of sampling error is plus or minus 3.3 percentage points.
"The president's lead continues to climb," Zogby said. He said Perot was also showing more strength.
Perot said again on Sunday on NBC's "Meet the Press" that he was in the race to stay despite Dole's plea last week that he drop out and endorse Dole.

Dole is campaigning in California on Sunday while Clinton, who stayed in Washington on Saturday to celebrate his wife Hillary's 49th birthday, appears in Virginia and Tennessee, the home state of Vice President Al Gore.
Poll respondents by narrow margins said they prefered Republicans to keep control of both the Senate and House.
